title: 6 Best Snowflake Frontend Builders in 2026
summary: Six ways to put an application frontend on Snowflake data, from Python apps inside your account to no-code builders.
body_markdown:
Snowflake started as a warehouse for analysts, and its default interface, Snowsight, reflects that. More teams now want to build applications on Snowflake data: account lookups for customer success, correction screens for finance, partner-facing views of shared data. That needs a frontend, and there are several ways to build one.


Below are six Snowflake frontend builders, with the point where each one stops. For SQL clients, see the[best Snowflake GUI tools](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/best-snowflake-gui-tools/) .


## The six options at a glance


Option Approach Viewers need Snowflake access? Cost


Jet Admin AI and visual builder on Snowflake No Free plan; paid tiers


Streamlit in Snowflake Python apps inside your account Yes Included; compute billed


Snowflake Native Apps Apps distributed to other Snowflake accounts Yes, in the consumer account Varies


Sigma BI with write-back Sigma users Paid


Retool Developer-built internal tools No Free tier; paid per user


Appsmith Open source internal tools No Free, open source; paid plans


## The options


### 1. Jet Admin


Jet Admin connects to Snowflake and builds a frontend on your tables and views: searchable lists, record pages, forms, approval steps and dashboards. You describe the app and Jet generates it, then refine it visually or with custom components and code. Jet queries Snowflake in place, on a warehouse you choose, so compute stays predictable.


People sign in to the app, not Snowflake, and roles decide which rows and fields each person sees. You can also combine Snowflake with operational databases and APIs in one app. Granular permissions, SSO and audit logs are on the Business plan and above; unlimited users are on every plan, including Free.


**Where it stops:** it is not a notebook or a place for ad hoc SQL analysis.


### 2. Streamlit in Snowflake


Data engineers write Python apps that run inside Snowflake, governed by Snowflake roles. It is the fastest path for Python teams.


**Where it stops:** every change is Python, and viewers need Snowflake access.


### 3. Snowflake Native Apps


The Native App Framework lets providers package data and logic, often with a Streamlit interface, and distribute it to other Snowflake accounts through the Marketplace.


**Where it stops:** it is built for data providers shipping apps to Snowflake customers, not for internal tools.


### 4. Sigma


Sigma is a spreadsheet-style BI tool on Snowflake with input tables that write data back.


**Where it stops:** it is analytics first, not operational screens with record pages and workflows.


### 5. Retool


Retool connects to Snowflake, and developers build internal tool frontends with components and JavaScript.


**Where it stops:** per-user pricing and developer maintenance.


### 6. Appsmith


Appsmith is open source and self-hostable with a Snowflake connector.


**Where it stops:** JavaScript-heavy apps for developers to maintain.


## Which to use


- **Business users need screens on Snowflake without Snowflake accounts:** Jet Admin.
- **Your data team writes Python and viewers already use Snowflake:** Streamlit in Snowflake.
- **You ship data products to other Snowflake customers:** Native Apps.
- **Analysts need write-back in BI:** Sigma.
- **Developers will build internal tools:** Retool or Appsmith.


## Start with who needs the data


If the audience is already in Snowflake, Streamlit is enough. If it is the rest of the company or your partners,[connect Snowflake to Jet Admin](https://www.jetadmin.io/integrations/snowflake) and give them a frontend without Snowflake seats.
